- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The best time to go on a river cruise in Europe is Spring (April to May), early summer (June), high season (July to August), Fall (September to October), and Winter (November to March).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spring and early summer are ideal for milder weather, blooming flora, lower prices, and fewer crowds, with temperatures ranging from 10 to 20°C (50-68°F).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] High season (July to August) is the busiest and most expensive, with temperatures around 25°C (77°F) and high humidity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Fall (September to October) is known for harvest season, stunning foliage, and fewer tourists, with temperatures ranging from 5 to 15°C (41-59°F).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Winter (November to March) has few river cruises available but can appeal to budget travelers wanting to experience Christmas markets and snow-covered landscapes, with temperatures ranging from -3 to 10°C (27-50°F).

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Danube River flows through ten countries and includes cities like Budapest, Vienna, and Bratislava.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Rhine River is known for its scenic beauty, vineyards, and castles, with destinations like Amsterdam, Cologne, and Strasbourg.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Douro River flows through Spain and Portugal, with destinations like Porto and Salamanca.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Rhone River offers experiences in the French countryside, with destinations like Avignon, Arles, and Lyon.
